log.reply:
# Practitioner Academy Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Format:** Two days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day
**Price:** US$12,500

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client's AI portfolio spans three stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year

The Client describes its AI maturity as Piloting. The stated regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, although the start date is not fixed.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. You stated the objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Profile Block lists two incumbent frameworks, an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. This proposal does not assume that any specific register, process, control or record exists under them. Whether either can be extended to AI governance is Unknown and will be tested during the program.

## 2. Why Practitioner Capability Fits Now

The Client has one system in production, one in pilot and one in planning. That combination lets practitioners build governance on live material instead of hypotheticals.

The visual inspection pilot has a stated production target of Q2 2027. That target gives the work a fixed horizon. The June 2026 audit finding also names a concrete first artifact: the inventory.

The Practitioner Academy places Legal, security, quality, data, operations and internal audit perspectives in the same working sessions. They build the first versions of the instruments together. The program follows three principles throughout: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

The Academy starts capability and artifacts. It does not by itself put governance in place, and it makes no certification or audit outcome promise, including for ISO/IEC 42001.

## 3. Running Worked Examples

Two use cases run through both days. The third appears at inventory and intake only.

**AI visual inspection, German production line (primary).** This example was selected for three reasons:
- It carries the stated Q2 2027 deadline.
- It requires an EU AI Act classification exercise. The classification outcome is Unknown until the exercise is done.
- It is subject to the stated constraint that the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

**Customer service chatbot (secondary).** This example was selected for three reasons:
- It is the one deployed system.
- It engages GDPR.
- It is bound by the stated constraint that customer data must stay in the EU.

**AI sales forecasting (intake only).** As a planned system, it is used to demonstrate how a system enters the inventory before build.

**Confidentiality approach.** All exercises use sanitized analogs. No real customer data, production staff data or production line records are used.
- **Chatbot exercises** use synthetic support transcripts.
- **Visual inspection exercises** use written specifications of a synthetic inspection task with no staff identifiers.

The works council constraint is recorded as an implementation dependency in every artifact touching visual inspection. The current consultation status is Unknown.

## 4. Curriculum Spine and Exercises

The program draws on four frameworks:

- **Day 1:** GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- **Day 2:** Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen), plus assurance work
- **Acceptance reference:** The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done)
- **Sponsor reporting reference:** AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards)

Module and pattern names below follow the curriculum spine. Exact file paths will be confirmed in the pre-work packet.

| Session | Exercise | Module, pattern or kit section | Artifact produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 S1 | *The Turtle and the Phoenix*, told from the facilitation kit (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md). The handle map links the story to the workbook modules. Closes with the kit's twenty-minute closing exercise. | Facilitation kit: story, handle map, section 8 closing exercise | The three artifacts specified in section 8 of the kit |
| D1 S1 | Map who decides, approves and is accountable for AI at the Client. Owners not yet decided are rendered Unknown. | GRC Workbook: governance structures | Draft AI governance roles and decision-rights map |
| D1 S2 | Enter all three systems with stage, purpose and jurisdiction. Run a first-pass EU AI Act classification for each. | GRC Workbook: AI system inventories and classification | Started AI system inventory with draft classifications |
| D1 S3 | Assess risks and impacts for visual inspection and the chatbot, including GDPR and EU data residency. Record the works council dependency. | GRC Workbook: risk and impact assessments | Draft risk register entries for both systems |
| D1 S4 | Draft a policy outline and one operating procedure gating the pilot-to-production transition for visual inspection. | GRC Workbook: policies and operating procedures | Draft AI policy outline; draft production-gate procedure |
| D2 S1 | Specify governed prompts for the chatbot on synthetic transcripts. Build the answer and escalation flow. | Slow AI Kitchen: governed prompting | Governed workflow 1: chatbot answer and escalation |
| D2 S2 | Design the inspection result and human disposition flow on the synthetic inspection specification. | Slow AI Kitchen: practical AI workflow design | Governed workflow 2: visual inspection disposition |
| D2 S3 | Assign human sign-off points across both workflows. Set acceptance criteria against The Definition of Done. | Slow AI Kitchen: human oversight and accountability | Oversight and sign-off matrix; draft acceptance criteria |
| D2 S4 | Link each artifact to the audit question it answers. Draft the intake record for sales forecasting. Outline a sponsor summary using AI Governance for Boards. | Evidence collection and audit readiness | Evidence map; forecasting intake record; sponsor summary outline |

## 5. Deliverables

Participants leave with working drafts in the two repositories:

- **Governance foundations:** the three section 8 fable artifacts and a decision-rights map
- **Inventory:** a started AI system inventory covering all three systems
- **Risk register:** draft entries for visual inspection and the chatbot
- **Policy:** a draft policy outline and a production-gate procedure
- **Governed workflows:** two governed workflows, one for chatbot answers and escalation and one for visual inspection disposition
- **Oversight:** an oversight and sign-off matrix with draft acceptance criteria
- **Assurance:** an evidence map, a forecasting intake record and a sponsor summary outline

Who owns finishing each artifact after the program is Unknown. It will be assigned in the closing session.

## 6. Logistics and Price

**Format:** Two days, live virtual, each day structured as four 90-minute working sessions.

**Audience:** The program is designed for the roles listed in the Profile Block:
- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- Two internal auditors

**Scheduling:** Participant names, dates and time zones are Unknown and will be confirmed before scheduling.

**Price:** US$12,500. For reference, the stated budget constraint is US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 7. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. To keep that date workable, we propose a 30-minute call to confirm three things:

1. Participant list
2. Program dates
3. Whether the sanitized analog approach meets the Client's confidentiality requirements

The pre-work packet follows confirmation.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: D2 S4 lists the module as "Evidence collection and audit readiness" without a GRC Workbook or Slow AI Kitchen prefix. The other rows carry a prefix. I treated the spine topic name as a named repository asset because the response says module names follow the curriculum spine, and the system prompt places evidence collection under Day 2 (Slow AI Kitchen plus assurance). Another scorer could decide this row does not name a specific repository asset and fail item 4.

Statements that the chatbot engages GDPR and that visual inspection is subject to the works council constraint are consequences of stated drivers and constraints applied to stated systems. Under the v1.14.3 guidance they are not new Client facts.
"A stated production target of Q2 2027" for the pilot comes from the sponsor's quoted objective. I treated it as stated, not inferred.
